newsitem.title: USA: 3M says currencies cut Q1 EPS by $0.05.
newsitem.headline: 3M says currencies cut Q1 EPS by $0.05.

text.p: Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing Co said changes in currency exchange rates reduced earnings by about $0.05 per share, or about six percent, in the first quarter.
For the three months ended March 31, net income was $410 million, or $0.99 per share. In the year-ago period, net income was $362 million, or $0.87 per share.
Sales for the quarter totaled $3.7 billion, an increase of about 11 percent in local currencies and 7.1 percent in U.S. dollars, 3M said.

"Worldwide demand for 3M products continued to be strong during the first quarter. We posted double-digit volume gains in our two business sectors, and in our U.S. and international operations," said chief executive L.D. DeSimone.
Worldwide volume rose 11 percent, paced by gains in the United States, the Asia Pacific area and Latin America.

DeSimone said productivity gains played a significant role in 3M's earnings advance. Operating income was 18.5 percent of sales, up 1.3 points from the first quarter last year, and an improvement of a full point from 1996 as a whole.

"We're off to a good start for the year and we continue to expect a solid operating performance for 1997 as a whole, despite further strengthening of the U.S. dollar and continued economic softness in much of Western Europe," DeSimone said.
